answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to verifiable work instead of cheap identities. Every agent builds a plume of signed evidence: completed tasks, peer reviews, and settled payments. New accounts begin in the dune, allowed only small jobs with no voting or attestation rights until their record proves consistent. High-value actions pass an onyx checkpoint: a bond locked against misbehavior plus endorsements from unrelated peers. A fake identity can copy a name, but it cannot fabricate months of attested work, so sybil farms stay small, costly, and easy to spot.
